content:
Currently, the definition of LeftOrdContinuous requires that if a bottom element exists, the function preserves the bottom element, and similarly for a top element. This means that Continuous does not necessarily imply LeftOrdContinuous on conditionally complete lattices with a bottom or top – e.g. f : ℝ≥0 → ℝ≥0 defined by f x = x + 1 is continuous but not left continuous.

I can’t quite tell if this how intentional this is. The only use I could find of LeftOrdContinuous elsewhere in Mathlib is just a synonym for some_order_iso.isLUB_image'. Intuitively, I would expect that “continuous iff left- and right-continuous” holds, but maybe I’m wrong here?
these definitions were added in their current form in mathlib3#2886
let's ask @Yury G. Kudryashov who is listed as an author

hmm, the original definitions prior to mathlib3#2886 were added in mathlib3#4, a PR which also added a lot of other stuff, but then they were only used one time in that same PR outside of the place they were defined, in order to conclude that the coercion from uniform space to topological space preserves binary suprema from the fact that it preserves arbitrary suprema (the orderings on uniform spaces and on topological spaces were backwards to how they are now)
I love how in the earliest days of Mathlib you could just add 3,000 lines of code and no one would find it weird
I also think we should remove this condition. It reminds me of how normal ordinal functions aren't required to satisfy f(0) = 0.
My only use case for this definition is the theorem about translation numbers.
If you modify the definition so that it works for my use case, then there won't be objections from me. Disclaimer: I don't know what people use in literature about orders etc.

I put up a PR that makes this change:
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/37682
And two PRs that depend on it, fleshing out the API for LeftOrdContinuous a bit:
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/37683
https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/37684

Violeta Hernández ha dicho:

I also think we should remove this condition. It reminds me of how normal ordinal functions aren't required to satisfy f(0) = 0.

In fact, with this redefinition, docs#Order.IsNormal would imply docs#LeftOrdContinuous. This theorem is exactly docs#Order.IsNormal.map_isLUB.
And in a linear order, the only difference between these two definitions is that LeftOrdContinuous implies Monotone, whereas IsNormal implies StrictMono.
To be completely clear, I'm not the arbiter of whether this is a good change and whether it goes into Mathlib. But I do personally like it.
